newsitem.title: USA: Prisoners exchanged in Texas standoff.
newsitem.headline: Prisoners exchanged in Texas standoff.

text.p: Armed separatists demanding independence for Texas released two hostages early on Monday in exchange for one of their members being set free from jail, officials said.

The self-designated Republic of Texas group released a married couple they had taken hostage at midday on Sunday and police released the Republic's chief of security, Bob Scheidt, less than 24 hours after he was arrested on weapons possession charges.
"The two hostages have been released to law enforcement officials," said Laureen Chernow, a spokeswoman for the Texas Department of Public Safety.

Republic of Texas members seized Joe and Margaret Rowe at their home near the separatist group's compound in the Davis Mountains of southwest Texas. The seizure came shortly after local police arrested Scheidt for carrying two assault rifles in his van.

During a tense 12-hour standoff, Republic leaders said they would only set free their hostages in return for the release of Scheidt and another group member who was recently arrested in Austin on contempt of court charges.
But police released only Scheidt. Chernow said it was not yet clear whether FBI agents and dozens of local and state police mobilized to surround the Republic's compound would be withdrawn.
